body_revisions.scope: A committed transaction through page/log persistence and a selected recovery target
body_revisions.observation: Nine full sections define rows, pages and redo/undo/binlog before crash recovery and point-in-time recovery. The consistent base, matching coordinate, actual ROW events and transaction stopping boundary precede the real MySQL replay and business acceptance.

body_revisions.scope: Source commit, replica application and new-write ownership
body_revisions.observation: Nine full sections connect row versions and RR/RC snapshots to the source, receive and apply chain, then GTID target/set checks, controlled write fencing and planned promotion. Independent capacity examples remain separate from the native fixture.

body_revisions.scope: One byte stream through framing, half-close and readiness-driven execution
body_revisions.observation: Nine complete sections follow socket ownership and one declared byte stream through sequence space, message framing, application response, flow control and nonblocking scheduling. LT/ET readiness and actual Linux epoll evidence retain separate protocols and scope.
